items.note: The plan gives the constants, both gate constructions, the eight-row schedule, the net change (JV+RG)x independent of the scratch values a,c, the bit and complex coefficient cancellations, the chain (x,y)->(x,y+x)->(-y,y+x)->(-y,x) and the wire counts, exactly as in the proof at 741-783.

The invariant (stored array = D_v applied to the logical array, from g=D_in^{-1}f), its passage along edges and through gates by commutation with a common frame, the operator D_out S_Omega D_in^{-1} and the route operator epsilon_w D_sink(rho(w)) D_source(w)^{-1} all match 804-825.

The bilinear spaces, terminal labels, interstage transitions, gate-label table, the nested side edge 2->5, the single decreasing edge 3->4 losing h (L=Ich), the telescoping to Wm-2N+2L, the orthonormal-basis argument and the ratios 100/539 and 101/539 all follow the paper. The full residual table at 1022-1042 is summarized rather than listed.

The projections P_U with -P_{U_a} at the X_a sources, the frames Phi_M, rank(P_V-P_U)=dim V-dim U, the N rank-one exceptions 2P_{U_a}, s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b<W_b m and the endpoint check P_{U_a^perp}+P_{U_a}=I_m reproduce 1115-1171.

The plan follows the proof: weight additivity mod 4 for orthogonal vectors, the phase difference as a sum over the residual basis, the conversion of each factor into aI+bX_v or its inverse, the count s_c=W_c m-2N+2L_c, the 27-coordinate fix-up via C=iZC^{-1}Z, and C^{otimes m} (or C^{otimes mk}) on every role.

L<N/2 with the exact ratios, the deficits eta_b=339/22587335000000 and eta_c=73/19906842167500 exceeding 20*2^{-50}, log m<20, and m^{1-2^{-50}}>m(1-20*2^{-50})>m(1-eta), giving s/W<m^tau with tau=sigma=1-2^{-50}, all match the paper.

S2 and S3 state the O(V) operations, and S3 even names the split-and-merge mechanism, but no sub-steps derive them. S2's 'streams of equal shape' omits the condition that W divides R, and S3's claim leaves out the b^{O(1)} offset-preparation condition, which appears only in its quote.

The plan follows the paper: the factorization A=E_1 Pi E_2 by topmost-row/rightmost-pivot elimination, a fixed odd prime avoiding the denominators and diagonal numerators, triangular transforms by controlled shifts in descending order, and one interchange per one of Pi through D_j+=H_i, swap, D_j=H_i-D_j.

The plan follows the paper: the cyclic row split into W role streams of volume V/W, Phi_{A_e} on each edge by recursive interchanges, H<-H+D on every row via the endpoint identity, the three-shear interchange, exactly s calls, F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1) solved by the geometric sum, and the fixed-tape parking and descriptor-stack schedule.

The plan gives the paper's choices of k and rho, the field-order sequence for exchanging and joining the high digits, R=q^{2rho}>=W^k padded to R'<2R, the base-m pieces costing O(V)sum a_j m^{j tau}=O(Ve^tau), the binary padding to [q^e] and the one-bit unequal-width case, as at 1649-1762.

The plan follows the paper: the identities for H_0 and C, the conjugation P_M X_v P_M^{-1}=X_{Mv} giving the coordinate form, slots of f chunks with one child per residual vector, inverse children via (-i)^f Z C Z, at most m(m-1)+3m row additions, exactly s_c child calls, and H_0^{otimes D}=b^D S_D C^{otimes D} S_D.

The headline bound O(V(L^tau+1)) is the lemma's simplification for the parameter family; S4.6.2.11-12 give the full time bound and the family conditions. The plan also has the eight-line cycle construction, the packed cyclic shifts, the guard set B with delta_bad=min{1,80(f-1)2^{-K}}, the repair permutation T_0 S_0^{-1} of B by extraction and radix sort, and the application to a change of basis.

The plan follows the paper: individual kernels at O(Ve), node overhead O(V((eK)^tau+1)), q_0 and k_0 with row padding, the role split u=Wg+w giving V/W children, the recurrence F(e)<=(s/W)F(e/m)+O((eK)^tau+1), and the internal-node and leaf sums with the base-m partition giving O(d^{lambda'}).

The guard-width constants E, B, nu, C_1=20, C_0=128mB^2, the depth recurrence A(e)<=sA(e/m)+E, depth converted to denominator and magnitude growth, Delta=o(p), the uniform packed-call cost and the single truncation with error <sqrt2 2^{-p} all follow 2450-2758.

The plan follows the paper: character cancellation via the shift by t/2^{v+1}, the decimation-in-frequency formula, bit-reversed storage B_t, the opposite procedure F_t^+B_t^{-1}, grouped rounds with J_E, the layout L from prefix-slot moves and K-chunk exchanges, the cost terms dK, pK^{tau-1} and l d^{lambda'}, one truncation per round, and the operators LBF^- and F^+B^{-1}L^{-1}.

The plan follows the proof: evaluation at B_0=2^{4p}, the separation |h_j|<=r2^{2p}<B_0/2, signed block encoding with carries in {-1,0}, centered extraction with the residual identity, negacyclic reduction giving |H_j|<=r2^{2p}, truncation by a shift of p+l bits, and four products costing O(rp log(rp)).

The plan follows 3414-3495: two forwards kept in the common LB order (pointwise products commute with a common record permutation), the normalization identity, the error chain 2delta+eta then 3delta+eta then M(3delta+eta)=sqrt2 M(3l+1)2^{-p}, and the cost with the log(rp) term.

The plan follows the paper: the maps S and T, the selection N=CTD with ||N-I||<1/2 and its Neumann inverse, the normalizations giving 2^{-2alpha^2}, A=S' and B_0=D'J'C with the quoted error and time bounds, the ordered generation of C, and the tensor form with linewise errors dp^2 and axis exposure O(Tpd^2(1+l^tau)). The record-format conversion at 3698-3792 is not covered, but it is not essential to the mathematics.

The plan follows 3938-3987: periodicity of the chirp, the coefficient comparison leaving exp(2 pi i sum s_i j_i k_i/t_i), Q reading frequency -s_i j_i, F_q^+R_c=R_c^{-1}F_q^+ giving RF^+R=F^+, and the two normalizations giving (u*v)/S^2.

The constants, sizes, alpha, gamma, eta, prime intervals, T/2<S<T, alpha^4 theta_i>p and the n^{o(1)} search match the paper. The plan omits the check that the fixed exponents satisfy the layer and margin conditions (4018-4036), and the derivation of eq:sizes with the comparison constants a_d, b_d, a_r, b_r, C_l (4067-4087).

The plan follows 4204-4292: the isomorphism argument (the image of x has order S), the triangular digit formula, padding insertion, the update order i=d,...,1, valid-interval rotations preserving the zero padding, and the O(d^2) unequal-width axis interchanges.

The plan follows the paper: well-definedness from (zeta y)^r=1, the diagonal isometric isomorphism, the wrap check zeta^{k+l}(-1)^h=zeta^j, M_C=D_- iota^{-1} M_r(iota D_+ f, iota D_+ g)=(f*g)/T, and the computed twist sequence with factor errors below 2*2^{-p}.

The plan follows the paper's procedures. Chirp numerators are computed modulo 2r, x_0, y_0 and C~ are as defined, the source transform composes A, the chirp transform, B_0 and the scale 2^gamma, and the opposite transform is obtained by conjugation. The plan also gives the scaled digits a_j 2^{-b-2}, the six steps, and the two occurrences of S undoing (u*v)/S^2 and the input scales.

The error chain E_ring<5TL, 6TL, 8TL, E_s=9*2^gamma TL, (2E_s+2), (3E_s+2), E_w<28*2^gamma T^2 L and the final bound 448b 2^{-3b/4}<1/2, with the disk margins, rounding and the carry recurrence with its invariant, all match 4557-4806.

The plan follows the paper: the seven table rows and their powers, the margins g_1..g_7 with minimum 2^{-181}=2 kappa, the per-row justifications, setup p^{A+C}=o(Tp), exceptional-stream sorting O(Vp^{A'}2^{-K})=o(V), absorption of log p powers into p^kappa, and the schoolbook cutoff.

S1 names the Schonhage-Strassen n log n conjecture and the power saving in the same model. No step gives the eventual-lower-bound formulation T_A(n)>=c_A n lg n, or the liminf negation that the bound refutes.

errors.says: The multiplication algorithm obtains the exact 2n-bit product 'in O(Tp) steps beyond the layer costs'.
errors.paper: Outside the butterfly layers several stages are superlinear in Tp: Gaussian line maps cost O(dTp^{3/2+delta}alpha), packed polynomial products O(Tp log(rp)), CRT and axis layouts O(Tpd^2(1+l^tau)), and chirps O(Tdp^{1+delta}) (Table tab:costs and its justification). Only input conversion, carries and similar scans are linear.

errors.says: The total dimension L lost on decreasing edges 'is L_b/N=100/539 and L_c/N=101/539, below N/2'.
errors.paper: L=Ich; it is the ratio L/N that equals 100/539 or 101/539 and is below 1/2, so L<N/2. The plan conflates L with L/N.

chain: The tree follows the paper's route end to end. It builds the scalar exchange network, puts frames on it and attaches subspace labels to bound s<Wm, then fixes the exponent tau=1-2^{-50}. From there it turns the bit and complex networks into the interchange and layer recurrences, and then goes through the synthetic transforms, ring convolution, resampling with permutation cancellation, assembly, exact recovery and the margin table to O(n(lg n)^{1-kappa}). The plan does not break anywhere. It is thinnest in three places: the elementary stream lemmas are only stated, the fixed exponents are never checked against the layer and margin conditions (4018-4036), and the S8 headline misstates the non-layer costs as linear.

steps.note: S4.1.1 gives h=100, v=161700, N=v^3 and m=h^3, with the banks indexed by triples. S4.1 and S4.1.9 give the fixed linear network sending (X_a,Y_a) to (-Y_a,X_a) and restoring every scratch wire whatever its initial value.

A common invertible frame per gate commutes with the pointwise gate, so the network implements D_out S_Omega D_in^{-1}. Each edge pays only D_v D_u^{-1}, and a route applies epsilon_w D_sink(rho(w)) D_source(w)^{-1}.

The labels are nondegenerate subspaces of F^{otimes 3} of dimension m, and the gate-label table is given. Every edge joins comparable labels, and the only decreasing edges are the central 3->4 edges, each losing h.
S4.3.6.3 shows P_V-P_U has rank dim V-dim U, and S4.3.6.4 gives the N source edges 2P_{U_a} as rank-one exceptions. For the complex network, S4.3.7 counts one kernel per residual basis vector.
The sum of absolute dimension changes is Wm-2N+2L with L=Ich, obtained by telescoping at gates with source total N and sink total Wm-N. This gives s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b.

L/N=100/539 and 101/539 are below 1/2, so after the extra N source ranks a strict saving remains: s_b<W_b m, and s_c<W_c m with deficit 2N-2L_c. The bit deficit N-2L_b is implied by these formulas rather than written out.

M_sink(rho(w))-M_source(w)=I_m holds for every role, checked as P_{U_a^perp}+P_{U_a}=I_m. Through the frame identity this makes the physical output Phi_{I_m}f_w, that is H<-H+D on every row, scratch rows included.
A shear by a rank-a matrix factors as E_1 Pi E_2 and costs exactly a interchanges plus O(V). Each edge is applied by recursive interchanges, so a node makes exactly s recursive calls.
Children have volume V/W, giving F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1). With s/W<m^tau, tau=1-2^{-50} from eta>20*2^{-50} and log m<20, the geometric sum gives F_k=O(e^tau).

central.summary: The plan reconstructs the whole central chain with its defining content: the fixed h=100 exchange network, the common frames, the nested labels with the only loss at the central 3->4 edges, rank equal to dimension change with N rank-one source exceptions, the budget Wm-2N+2L, L/N<1/2, the endpoint identity giving H<-H+D, edges as exactly s recursive calls, and the recurrence solved to O(e^tau) with tau=1-2^{-50}. All nine steps are reconstructed.
